name: Wolverine WVR-6R — silhouette study
notes: New independent WVR-6R silhouettes with left dorsal six-port rack and right forearm cannon. No inherited humanoid component generator. Shape review 2: remove inaccurate chest port mass, simplify shoulder launcher, keep forearm cannon smaller than whole chest. Reference iteration 3: independently traced ten-sided angular chest and forebody, sloped shoulder cowlings, tall rectangular six-port rack beside helmet, and narrow angular pilot helmet rather than bulbous cylinders. Reference iteration 4: broken-up wide shoulder shields, one clenched fist, distinctly separate cannon shroud in right arm, angular knee/thigh guards and narrower reverse-taper greaves. Fifth pass: separate armored hip section bridges chest and leg roots; individual six SRM bores remain on high asymmetric left launcher. Pass 6: individually framed six-port missile rack with physically carved 2x3 launch openings. Pass 7: hollow right-arm AC5 muzzle frame and hand with individually shaped knuckles and thumb, with no dangling fingers. Pass 8: replace rounded Wolverine torso masses with planar swept armor cowlings, bring shoulder pads closer to reference and reduce shared overlap along the shoulder seams. Shape pass 9: leaned chamfered pauldron armor, forward rectangular visor helmet and thin radio antennas, broad shouldered segmented chest. References WVR-6R FSW ink and multiple miniature viewpoints. Pass 10: replaced hollow-appearing pauldron caps with solid tapered shoulder-shell contours; split the single hexagonal chest into two swept structural breastplates.
